findings.title: Live and bandwidth polling can accumulate unresolved requests
findings.reachability: Confirmed whenever the page is visible and a live request exceeds five seconds or a bandwidth request exceeds sixty seconds.
findings.evidence_summary: Intervals call loaders without a fetch timeout; live has no abort/dedupe and bandwidth has no concurrency guard.
findings.impact: Slow or hanging responses can create growing in-flight request counts and unnecessary server/browser load.
findings.recommendation: Add bounded timeouts and one in-flight request per poller; abort or skip the previous request before starting another.

findings.title: Bandwidth refresh failure leaves prior card values presented as current
findings.reachability: Confirmed after at least one successful bandwidth render followed by a failed refresh.
findings.evidence_summary: The catch changes only `bandwidthStatus`; card text, timestamps, and `data-state` remain untouched.
findings.impact: Operators can read stale throughput and retransmit values without a per-card stale indication.
findings.recommendation: Track last success and pending/stale state; mark or clear every card when refresh fails while retaining an explicit last-known timestamp if desired.

findings.title: Live refresh failure preserves old legend values while its warning is hidden
findings.reachability: Confirmed after successful live data followed by a failed live poll.
findings.evidence_summary: The catch updates only `liveStatus`; previous legend values remain, and `master.css:49` sets `#liveStatus` to `display:none`.
findings.impact: Old latency values can appear current with no visible failure indicator.
findings.recommendation: Expose a visible stale state and associate freshness/timestamp with each legend or clear the values on failure.

findings.title: Latency failures can hide the error overlay
findings.reachability: Confirmed for a non-abort latency failure during initialization or interactive chart reload.
findings.evidence_summary: `finally` adds the hidden class; the outer catch later changes overlay HTML but does not remove that class.
findings.impact: The chart can remain empty or stale without an accessible visible failure state; interactive handlers may also reject without local recovery.
findings.recommendation: Own loading/error visibility in one state transition and catch interactive reload failures explicitly.

findings.title: Bandwidth selection assumes API rows are already newest-first
findings.reachability: Reachable for every bandwidth response containing duplicate server/direction rows; correctness depends on an undocumented order contract.
findings.evidence_summary: The first upload and download row per server win; rows are not sorted or compared by timestamp.
findings.impact: A changed or inconsistent response order can display an older sample as the latest result.
findings.recommendation: Define ordering in the API contract and independently select the newest valid timestamp in the client.

findings.title: Chart detail is pointer-only with no keyboard or textual equivalent
findings.reachability: Confirmed for keyboard-only and non-visual users of the latency trend.
findings.evidence_summary: The canvas has an aria-label, but tooltip interaction is bound only to pointer events and there is no fallback table or description.
findings.impact: Users who cannot operate or perceive the canvas cannot inspect historical measurements and failure points.
findings.recommendation: Provide a keyboard-focusable interaction and an equivalent textual/table representation of chart data.

findings.title: Unvalidated API shapes can interrupt initialization and rendering
findings.reachability: Reachable when a successful JSON response omits expected arrays/objects or contains invalid timestamps and numeric fields.
findings.evidence_summary: Loaders dereference response fields directly inside a two-stage `Promise.all`; only bandwidth normalizes alternate container shapes.
findings.impact: One malformed response can prevent the second initialization group, throw event-handler rejections, or leave partially updated UI.
findings.recommendation: Validate and normalize each endpoint response before mutation, and isolate section failures so one endpoint cannot block unrelated panels.

findings.title: Bandwidth success state token does not match the recovered CSS
findings.reachability: Confirmed whenever a bandwidth row is successful.
findings.evidence_summary: JavaScript writes `data-state=ready`, while `master.css:63` styles success as `data-state=ok`; disabled is also unstyled.
findings.impact: Successful cards retain the default gray state indicator instead of the intended success color.
findings.recommendation: Define one state enum shared by JavaScript and CSS and cover every enum value with a visual test.

findings.title: Bandwidth trend and empty-summary content remain permanently hidden
findings.reachability: Confirmed for all bandwidth states in the recovered document.
findings.evidence_summary: Both the trend parent and empty child have `hidden`; JavaScript updates the child but never clears either property.
findings.impact: The generated aggregate success/failure explanation is never visible.
findings.recommendation: Either remove dead rendering or explicitly model and test hidden/visible states.

findings.title: Route target fallback can recursively request without an explicit bound
findings.reachability: Reachable only if successive route responses repeatedly advertise nonempty target lists that exclude the echoed requested target.
findings.evidence_summary: The fallback selects the first target and immediately returns another `loadRoute()` with no retry count.
findings.impact: An inconsistent backend contract can cause a continuing serial request loop.
findings.recommendation: Allow at most one normalized-target retry and surface a contract error if the second response remains inconsistent.

findings.title: Overall status becomes an unvalidated class token
findings.evidence_summary: `overall.status` is concatenated into `className` rather than mapped through a known status enum.
findings.impact: Unexpected values can alter or remove intended status presentation, though this is not an HTML execution sink.
findings.recommendation: Map status through an explicit allowlist with a safe stale/unknown fallback.

findings.title: Dynamic status and segmented selection changes are not announced
findings.reachability: Confirmed for screen-reader users during live, route, loading, bandwidth, and filter updates.
findings.evidence_summary: Dynamic status nodes have no live-region semantics, and most selected buttons use only an `active` class.
findings.impact: State changes and current selections may not be perceivable without visual inspection.
findings.recommendation: Add appropriate `aria-live`/status roles and `aria-pressed` or a correct tab/selection pattern.

findings.title: Static document does not declare CSP or resource integrity
findings.reachability: Applies to the recovered HTML; deployment response headers were not part of TP-02A.
findings.evidence_summary: The same-origin CSS and JS tags have no integrity attribute and no CSP meta policy is present.
findings.impact: No exploit is established from this evidence alone; protection may be supplied by HTTP headers or a future proxy.
findings.recommendation: Define CSP and asset-integrity policy at the final deployment boundary after confirming framing and proxy requirements.

findings.title: No confirmed executable DOM injection path was found
findings.reachability: Covers all statically identified HTML sinks in the recovered script.
findings.evidence_summary: API strings entering HTML are escaped; other sink values are static, numeric, Intl-formatted, or constrained to known WAN metadata.
findings.impact: Static review found no direct DOM XSS, but fixture payloads should verify the assumptions at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Prefer DOM construction and `textContent` for future changes and retain malicious-string regression fixtures.

findings.title: Local storage is limited to a resilient preference value
findings.reachability: Read at script evaluation and written after VPS selection.
findings.evidence_summary: One VPS-selection key is used; exceptions are caught and the value is later normalized against the target catalog.
findings.impact: No sensitive persistence was found; an invalid value can only affect early preference state before normalization.
findings.recommendation: Keep the allowlist normalization and consider logging non-sensitive storage failures during diagnostics.

findings.title: Recovered production document still labels itself as candidate port 3003
findings.reachability: Always visible in the recovered footer.
findings.evidence_summary: The static footer retains candidate and port-3003 wording in the production-derived evidence.
findings.impact: The label can mislead operators and confirms deployment/documentation drift, but it is not a security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Move environment identity to release metadata and remove hardcoded port/version wording from canonical UI copy.
